module_title: Constitutional Bodies - Powers, Functions, and Independence
introduction: At this level, we look at the specific powers, the removal processes, and the collaborative roles these bodies play in the Indian democracy. These bodies are designed to be immune to political pressure from the executive.

core_concepts.title: Removal Process
core_concepts.description: The Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and the CAG can be removed ONLY in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court (by a special majority of both Houses of Parliament).

core_concepts.title: Multi-member Election Commission
core_concepts.description: Currently, the Election Commission consists of one Chief Election Commissioner and two other Election Commissioners. All three have equal power, salary, and status (equivalent to an SC Judge).

core_concepts.title: Advisory Role of UPSC
core_concepts.description: UPSC is primarily an advisory body. While the government must consult it on disciplinary matters and recruitment methods, it is not bound to accept the UPSC's advice (though it must explain its reasons to Parliament if it doesn't).

core_concepts.title: Audit Function of CAG
core_concepts.description: The CAG audits all expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India, the Consolidated Fund of each State, and the Contingency Fund. It checks for 'Propriety Audit'—meaning whether the expenditure is wasteful or wise.

important_entities.name: Public Accounts Committee (PAC)
important_entities.significance: The CAG is called the 'Friend, Philosopher, and Guide' of the PAC. The PAC examines the audit reports submitted by the CAG to the President.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: While the CEC has protection, the 'other' Election Commissioners can be removed by the President simply on the recommendation of the CEC.
The Chairman of UPSC and the CAG are ineligible for any further office under the Government of India or any State after they retire, to ensure their neutrality while in office.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Linking recruitment (UPSC-315) and election (EC-324) helps in chronological memorization of the Constitution's parts.

exam_strategy_tips: Note that for 'State Public Service Commissions', the retirement age is 62, whereas for UPSC, it is 65.
